title: Duke Energy takes down hundreds of fake websites, social media accounts and ads to help protect customers
summary: Duke Energy has removed hundreds of fake websites, social media accounts and online ads since November 2025 as part of an expanded effort to protect customers from increasingly sophisticated utility scams.
body_markdown:
-


### **AI-supported tool helps find fake content that could mislead customers**


-


### **Three steps help customers protect their money: spot it, check it and report it**


CHARLOTTE, N.C. – Duke Energy has removed hundreds of fake websites, social media accounts and online ads since November 2025 as part of an expanded effort to protect customers from increasingly sophisticated utility scams.


Many of these scams are designed to look like legitimate Duke Energy content, directing customers to fake payment pages and phone numbers.


Ahead of Utility Scam Awareness Day on Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026, Duke Energy, Piedmont Natural Gas and the Better Business Bureau are sharing three steps customers can use anytime something doesn’t feel right to protect their money and personal information: spot it, check it and report it.


“If something doesn’t feel right, take a moment to check your account at duke-energy.com, in the Duke Energy app or with the number on your bill, and report anything suspicious,” said Jessica Bednarcik, senior vice president of customer services operations at Duke Energy.


**How is Duke Energy helping protect customers from fake online content?**


Utility scams often begin when customers searching online for help find a fake customer service number posted across websites, social media, ads or apps. Duke Energy’s AI-supported tool scans websites, social media and paid ads for fake Duke Energy content, including impostor helplines. When the tool finds suspected scam content, Duke Energy works with the website or social media platform hosting it to have it removed.


In North Carolina, customers reported more than a thousand scam attempts to Duke Energy from January through September 2026.


**How can customers spot, check and report a utility scam?**


- Step 1 – Spot it: Pause when something doesn’t look right, especially when there is pressure to act now.


- Step 2 – Check it: Use the phone number or website on your Duke Energy or Piedmont Natural Gas bill – not a link, QR code or number from a search result or message.


- Step 3 – Report it: Don’t engage. Save the message, receipt or screenshot, then use Duke Energy’s[Scam Reporting Tool](https://scam-tool-web.duke-energy.app/home) or call[Piedmont Natural Gas](https://www.piedmontng.com/our-company/safety-information/id-protection-fraud-alerts) to report the suspicious content. When reporting a phone scam, include the number the scammer directed you to call. Don’t rely on the incoming number shown on caller ID because it can be spoofed.


**What you can count on from Duke Energy and Piedmont Natural Gas:** Duke Energy and Piedmont Natural Gas will never threaten to cut off your service right away or tell you how you must pay. Duke Energy never requires payment by prepaid card, cryptocurrency or a third-party payment app.


**If you have already paid or shared information:** You’re not alone, and acting quickly can help. Call your bank, change any affected passwords and report it at[reportfraud.ftc.gov](https://reportfraud.ftc.gov/) .


What partners say about protecting customers from scams


“Scammers will go to great lengths to steal your money or personal information, often using high-pressure tactics, secrecy and unusual payment methods to deceive their victims. Recognizing these warning signs is key to protecting yourself,” said **Juliana O’Rork, vice president marketing, communications & business development, BBB Greater Charlotte & Western NC** . “At BBB, we’re committed to helping consumers and businesses stay informed by sharing valuable insights and reports submitted through[BBB Scam Tracker](https://urldefense.proofpoint.com/v2/url?u=https-3A__www.bbb.org_scamtracker&d=DwMGaQ&c=euGZstcaTDllvimEN8b7jXrwqOf-v5A_CdpgnVfiiMM&r=p1JOuKAgxA9yf7f0J6FTsFVg1yBCUSy4LT8CTA0CcvA&m=qU9iWKGa6JjRdjFk-c3t6TzZq81Fvv_XdoZolcRVnPYGE1Q5A6Mv7VkHCl3FRBWZ&s=MshLIOtNDjBlvz6Nidee_FQaFo5K-Pg4j72ZrWnFz7U&e=) , empowering them to recognize potential scams before becoming victims.”


“Scammers often reach out when people are busy or worried about a bill,” said **Emily Henson, president of Piedmont Natural Gas** . “If a message about your natural gas account makes you uneasy, you never have to decide on the spot. Contact us using the number on your bill or through your online account, and our team can help you check.”


About Utilities United Against Scams (UUAS):[UUAS](https://www.utilitiesunited.org/) is a consortium of more than 150 U.S. and Canadian utilities that share data and best practices to protect customers. Utility Scam Awareness Day is a national effort led by UUAS, now in its 11th year.


**Duke Energy**


Duke Energy (NYSE: DUK), a Fortune 150 company headquartered in Charlotte, N.C., is one of America’s largest energy holding companies. The company’s electric utilities serve 8.7 million customers in North Carolina, South Carolina, Florida, Indiana, Ohio and Kentucky, and collectively own 55,700 megawatts of energy capacity. Its natural gas utilities serve 1.6 million customers in North Carolina, South Carolina, Ohio and Kentucky.


Duke Energy is executing an energy modernization strategy, keeping customer value at the forefront as it invests in electric grid upgrades and efficient generation resources to strengthen the system and serve growing energy needs.


More information is available at[duke-energy.com](http://www.duke-energy.com/) . Follow Duke Energy on X, LinkedIn, Instagram, TikTok and Facebook for stories about the people and innovations powering its communities.


**Piedmont Natural Gas**


Piedmont Natural Gas, a subsidiary of Duke Energy, distributes natural gas to more than 1 million residential, commercial, industrial and power generation customers in North Carolina and South Carolina. More information:[piedmontng.com](https://www.piedmontng.com/home) . Follow Piedmont Natural Gas:[Facebook](http://www.facebook.com/PiedmontNG) .


**Better Business Bureau**
The Better Business Bureau has empowered people to find businesses, brands, and charities they can trust for more than 110 years. In 2024, people turned to BBB.org more than 220 million times for BBB Business Profiles on 5.5 million businesses, and 725,000 times for BBB charity reports on 12,000 local and national charities. Regional, independent BBBs can be found across the United States and Canada, including BBB of Southern Piedmont and Western North Carolina, which was founded in 1949 and serves 37 counties in North Carolina and South Carolina.
